one_line: Pallava king of Kanchipuram, a warrior-innovator who championed rock-cut temples, drama and music c. 600–630 CE.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, lean but broad-shouldered, athletic build with the calm bearing of a seasoned ruler.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, warm medium-brown South Indian complexion, sharp brows, neatly trimmed moustache and short beard framing his jaw; eyes large and perceptive, default expression a thoughtful, confident half-smile as if weighing ideas and strategy.
appearance.hair: Thick, wavy black hair gathered into a modest high knot at the back of the crown, front kept tidy with a short center part; adorned with a simple gold circlet-band resting above the forehead, set with a single small dark red cabochon at the center.
appearance.costume: He wears a finely draped white cotton upper cloth (uttariya) over both shoulders and across the chest, with a pale gold border, paired with a calf-length deep maroon silken lower garment (dhoti-style veshti) wrapped securely and pleated in front, its hem edged with a thin dark green stripe; on his torso a fitted, sleeveless pale cream angavastra-like vest gives a regal yet practical look, while his arms bear plain gold armlets and slim bangles, and his neck carries a single medium-length gold chain with a small, round pendant; his feet are in simple dark brown leather sandals, and overall the fabrics are smooth, with subtle horizontal striping in the dhoti to suggest fine weaving, avoiding heavy ornamentation to emphasize intellectual refinement over ostentatious luxury.
appearance.signature: A rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin cord and tucked into his left hand, while his right hand rests lightly on the hilt of a plain steel sword with a gently curved blade and simple gold-capped wooden grip sheathed at his hip, the manuscript clearly emphasized as his primary prop.

ref_desc: Mahendravarman I is a mid-30s, medium-brown Pallava king with wavy black hair in a high knot, gold circlet, white cloth and cream vest over a deep maroon dhoti, gold ornaments, carrying a palm-leaf manuscript and simple sword in white, maroon, pale gold and dark green tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Mahendravarman I: a mid-30s South Indian Pallava king with an oval, thoughtful face, medium-brown complexion, sharp brows, and a neat moustache with short beard. His thick black hair is tied in a modest high knot at the back of the crown, front parted slightly, and he wears a simple gold circlet-band with a small dark red stone at the center. Show him in a historically grounded early-7th-century Pallava costume: a white cotton upper cloth draped over both shoulders and across the chest with a pale gold border, a fitted sleeveless pale cream vest on the torso, and a calf-length deep maroon dhoti-style veshti wrapped and pleated in front, hem edged with a thin dark green stripe and subtle horizontal weave lines. Add plain gold armlets, slim bangles, and a single medium-length gold chain with a small round pendant, plus simple dark brown leather sandals. In his left hand he prominently holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin cord, while his right hand rests lightly on the hilt of a plain steel sword with gently curved blade and gold-capped wooden grip sheathed at his hip, with the manuscript clearly the main prop. Use a palette dominated by white, deep maroon, pale gold, dark green and medium brown, and keep the overall design dignified, scholarly and martial, ready to be redrawn consistently in many panels.
